text:
ops-bot: ALERT: apiserver 5xx spike and controller-manager restarts in us-central2 (observed 14:20 UTC)
sam: seeing a ton of etcd follower disconnects around 14:18-14:22, leader staying but proposals queue up
priya: stacktrace from controller-manager: `etcdserver: request timed out` then OOMKilled on kube-controller-manager (heap growth from queued retries)
nikhil: pulled etcd raft logs: 
```
2025-10-12T14:18:04.321Z rafthttp: stream for peer 3: EOF
2025-10-12T14:18:05.102Z etcdserver: publish error: raft: failed to send to peer 3: write tcp 10.2.1.7:2380->10.2.1.9:2380: write: connection reset by peer
2025-10-12T14:18:12.678Z etcdserver: apply entry err: etcdserver: request timed out
```
neteng: telemetry shows huge SYN retries and NAT ephemeral exhaustion on nat-gw-us-central2-1 at 14:17-14:20
sam: why so many concurrent connections? any large fanout?
priya: model onboarding jobs ramped up 120->480 parallel pulls (autoscaler hook) to bring new GPU nodes online for a heavy training run
nikhil: registry retry storms from flaky mirrors + parallel pulls cause many ephemeral ports to be consumed (per-conn NAT mapping)
platform-bot: metric snapshot -> `curl -s http://monitoring.internal/us-central2/nat | jq '.ephemeral_port_utilization'` returns 0.98
sre-oncall: confirmed controller-manager crashloops on 2 control-plane nodes, apiserver 5xx rate peaked at 28%
neteng: overlay note: our per-flow SNAT map reached high cardinality and the NAT software started dropping new mappings rather than queuing -> asymmetric egress -> TCP resets
priya: timeline correlates: autoscaler created 40 GPU nodes at 14:10, onboarding controller kicked off shard pulls at 14:12, nat utilization spike 14:17, etcd follower RTT spike 14:18
sam: etcd follower rtt histograms: p95 jumped from 40ms -> 1.2s during event
nikhil: suggestion: immediately reduce pull concurrency, cordon new nodes, and set registry retry backoff to exponential + jitter
sre-oncall: mitigation step 1: cordon gpu-onboard-*-batch nodes (executing now)
sre-oncall: mitigation step 2: scale-down gpu-onboard-asg by 50% and pause onboarding jobs
platform-bot: applied temporary admission-webhook patch to set imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent for onboarding namespace (quick win)
neteng: opened cloud support case for ephemeral pool increase (case #CLD-42177) ETA 45m, also provisioning additional NAT gateway as standby
priya: after cordon and scale down, apiserver 5xx dropped to ~6% in 90s, controller-manager stable but we saw a backlog of failed reconciliation loops to clear
sam: root cause (prelim): onboarding fanout + registry retries -> SNAT port exhaustion -> TCP resets to etcd followers -> proposal timeouts -> apiserver 5xx and controller-manager OOM/restarts as control loops retry
ikhil: added nuance: regional load-balancer healthchecks were pinned to single NAT gw which amplified the failure domain; need better LB-to-NAT distribution
sre-oncall: created ticket SRE-2025-1900 and assigned to platform + networking: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-2025-1900
priya: proposed action items: [1] add pull-fanout cap in onboarding controller (default 8) [2] registry client: exponential backoff + jitter and circuit-breaker for persistent failures [3] NAT autoscale + ephemeral pool alerting at 75% [4] LB/NAT distribution review to avoid single gw hot spots [5] run chaos test to simulate egress saturation during onboarding
neteng: also propose short-term: reserve 2x NAT gateways for heavy model onboarding windows and add per-project egress quotas to avoid cross-tenant bleed
platform-bot: will submit PR to onboarding controller with pull cap flag and rollout plan (target: patch in 4 hours)
sam: let's also document rollback steps: 1) cordon node set 2) disable onboarding job in k8s 3) scale down ASG 4) flip registry mirrors to low-fanout mirror pool
sre-oncall: monitoring dashboard updated with alert rule `nat_ephemeral_utilization > 0.75 for 2m` and `etcd_proposal_latency > 500ms`
priya: will follow up with a short postmortem once we have cloud case closure and PR merged. tagging neteng for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
